figure: Pull-quote callout (unnumbered), lower third of page
issue: The pull-quote's own numbers contradict the linear law it states. It claims '2·70B · L tokens scales linearly — ~0.28 PFLOP at 1K → ~4.5 PFLOP at 32K'. Under 2·70B·L, L=1,000 gives 1.4e14 FLOP = 0.14 PFLOP, not 0.28; and 0.28 PFLOP scaled linearly to 32K would be 8.96 PFLOP, not 4.5. The 32K value (4.59 PFLOP) and the canonical 9.2K value (1.29 PFLOP) are both correct under 2·70B·L, so the '1K' figure is the sole outlier and is 2x too high. A reader who trusts the callout will mis-estimate prefill cost at short context by a factor of two.
evidence: Pull-quote: 'Prefill FLOP also grows with context: 2·70B · L tokens scales linearly — ~0.28 PFLOP at 1K → ~4.5 PFLOP at 32K for a 70B model ... the canonical 9.2K point the prefill is ~1.29 PFLOP (Table 8-1).' Recomputation: 2 x 70e9 x 1000 = 1.4e14 FLOP = 0.14 PFLOP; 2 x 70e9 x 32768 = 4.59e15 = 4.59 PFLOP; 2 x 70e9 x 9200 = 1.288e15 = 1.29 PFLOP (matches the printed 1.29). Ratio check: 4.5 / 0.28 = 16.1, but 32K / 1K = 32.
acceptance_test: The callout's 1K value equals 2 x 70e9 x 1000 / 1e15 = 0.14 PFLOP, and the printed pair (0.14 PFLOP at 1K, 4.5 PFLOP at 32K) satisfies the stated 32x linear ratio. The 9.2K value remains 1.29 PFLOP and agrees with Table 8-1.

figure: FIGURE 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The HDR series is labelled with a bandwidth basis that contradicts the figure's own title and the ring model's byte count. The figure title promises 'directional bandwidth' and the ring model divides one-directional per-rank sent bytes (245 GB) by a bandwidth, but the legend entry reads 'Two-way HDR: assumed effective 40 GB/s' and the caption repeats 'an assumed effective two-way HDR path'. 'Two-way' in interconnect usage means bidirectional aggregate. If it is read that way, the denominator is a bidirectional figure applied to a unidirectional byte count and the HDR ring time is understated by 2x (245 GB / 20 GB/s per direction = 12.25 s, not 6.125 s). The book's own definition on printed 157 is different again: 'a realistic effective throughput is roughly 40 GB/s (aggregated across 2 HDR rails/ports per node)'. So the number is right but the label names the wrong quantity, and the caption reinforces the wrong term.
evidence: Figure legend: 'Two-way HDR: assumed effective 40 GB/s'; figure header: 'HDR 6,125 ms'; caption: '40 GB/s for an assumed effective two-way HDR path'. Title: 'Ring traffic and directional bandwidth'. Printed 157: 'A realistic effective throughput is roughly 40 GB/s (aggregated across 2 HDR rails/ports per node — the multi-rail effective throughput referenced in §9.2 and Fig 9.1)'. Printed 157 also states HDR payload is '25 GB/s in both link coding', i.e. 25 GB/s per direction, 50 GB/s bidirectional, so 40 GB/s 'two-way' would be 20 GB/s per direction.
acceptance_test: The legend entry, the figure header, and the caption all state the same basis in words that cannot be read two ways, e.g. 'HDR, 2 rails, per-direction effective 40 GB/s'. A reader who computes 245 GB / 40 GB/s = 6.1 s from the figure alone reproduces the printed 6,125 ms, and a reader who reads the label as bidirectional can no longer derive 12.25 s from it. The figure title's word 'directional' is then true of all three series.
